title: 2nd Stopping Place 1st Truth Grandeur And Sublimity

questions.question: What is the main topic of the first truth in this passage?
questions.answer: It is about Allah’s greatness and majesty.

questions.question: Why does the passage give only a short explanation of the first truth here?
questions.answer: Because fuller proofs are said to be explained in other places.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the One who made the stars that are very far apart?
questions.answer: He creates and manages them together at the same time and in the same way.

questions.question: What example from plants shows wide control over the earth?
questions.answer: Many flowers of the same kind are made across all directions of the world at the same time.

questions.question: About how many kinds of plants and animals are mentioned as being cared for each spring?
questions.answer: More than two hundred thousand kinds.

questions.question: How long does the passage say this spring work takes?
questions.answer: About five or six weeks.

questions.question: What qualities describe this springtime work?
questions.answer: It is done with order, balance, and without mix-up, flaw, or mistake.

questions.question: What big event does spring remind people of in the passage?
questions.answer: It reminds people of a great bringing-to-life and shows Allah’s power clearly.

questions.question: What earlier act of creation is mentioned as another sign of Allah’s power?
questions.answer: The creation of the heavens and the earth in six days.

questions.question: What daily change is given as another example of Allah’s rule?
questions.answer: He brings night into day and day into night.

questions.question: Besides running the universe, what does the passage say Allah knows in people?
questions.answer: He knows the hidden thoughts in human hearts.

questions.question: When the passage says these many works are really one act, what idea is it teaching?
questions.answer: It teaches that one single Doer is behind them all.

questions.question: What does the passage conclude about the One doing these works?
questions.answer: He is one, powerful, and too majestic to have any partner.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does assigning partners to Allah wrongly suggest about Him?
questions.answer: It suggests weakness, need, fault, defect, and limits.

questions.question: Why would no sound mind accept partnership with Allah, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Because it goes against His perfect power, greatness, and complete rule.

questions.question: Why is shirk described as a very serious sin here?
questions.answer: Because it offends Allah’s glory, greatness, and majesty.

questions.question: What does the quoted Qur’anic warning say Allah does not forgive?
questions.answer: It says He does not forgive setting up partners with Him.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the second truth?
questions.answer: Allah’s lordly actions in the universe are absolute, wide-reaching, and seen everywhere.

questions.question: What limits these actions, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Only Allah’s wisdom and will, along with the abilities of the things and places involved.

questions.question: Which false explanations are rejected as causes of these ordered works?
questions.answer: Chance, nature, blind force, unconscious causes, and scattered elements.

questions.question: If those things are not true makers, what role does the passage give them?
questions.answer: They are only used as outward coverings by Allah’s command, will, and power.

questions.question: How many examples does the passage say will be given for the second truth?
questions.answer: Three examples.

questions.question: What title is given to the first truth in this passage?
questions.answer: It is called the truth of grandeur and sublimity.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the style in which stars are created and governed?
questions.answer: They are handled together in one time and one pattern.

questions.question: Which living thing is used as an example of being spread across east, west, north, and south?
questions.answer: Flowers of the same kind.

questions.question: What season is used to show Allah’s careful management of living things?
questions.answer: Spring.

questions.question: What does the passage say happens to huge numbers of plant and animal kinds in spring?
questions.answer: They are cared for, given life, separated by kind, and beautified.

questions.question: What does the passage stress about mistakes in this huge work?
questions.answer: It says there is no confusion, defect, or error in it.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention many examples of resurrection in spring?
questions.answer: To show Allah’s power to bring life again.

questions.question: What movement of the earth is mentioned in the first truth?
questions.answer: The earth is made to turn.

questions.question: What picture does the passage give for the night after the earth turns?
questions.answer: Night is like a page where the day’s events are written.

questions.question: What hidden part of human life does Allah manage too?
questions.answer: The secret thoughts in people’s hearts.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn from these many actions being treated as one action?
questions.answer: One unique and mighty Being does them all.

questions.question: What does the passage say Allah’s greatness leaves no room for?
questions.answer: It leaves no room at all for partners.

questions.question: What does Allah’s perfect greatness do to the idea of partnership?
questions.answer: It removes that idea completely.

questions.question: If someone gives Allah a partner, what wrong things are they acting as if Allah has?
questions.answer: They act as if He has weakness, need, imperfection, and limits.

questions.question: How does the passage describe a mind that would accept such an idea?
questions.answer: It says a sound mind would never accept it.

questions.question: Why is shirk not just a small mistake in this passage?
questions.answer: Because it insults Allah’s majesty and glory.

questions.question: What message from the Qur’an is used to show how serious shirk is?
questions.answer: The message that Allah does not forgive associating partners with Him, while lesser sins may be forgiven.

questions.question: What three qualities of Allah’s deeds begin the second truth?
questions.answer: Their absolute nature, their broad reach, and their appearing without limit.

questions.question: In the second truth, who alone controls and measures these deeds?
questions.answer: Allah alone, by His wisdom and will.

questions.question: Why can random events not be the source of these deeds?
questions.answer: Because the deeds are balanced, wise, life-giving, orderly, and firm.

questions.question: Why can nature and blind force not explain these works?
questions.answer: Because they have no understanding or wisdom to produce such careful results.

questions.question: What are chance and natural causes compared to in relation to Allah’s power?
questions.answer: They are like an outer covering that hides His power from direct view.

questions.question: What is the first truth trying to help the reader understand about Allah?
questions.answer: It helps the reader understand Allah’s unmatched greatness and majesty.

questions.question: Why does the passage move quickly through the first truth instead of fully expanding it?
questions.answer: Because detailed proofs are said to be found elsewhere.

questions.question: What does the example of the same type of flower around the world show?
questions.answer: It shows that Allah creates in the same way everywhere on earth.

questions.question: Why is the number of plant and animal kinds important in the argument?
questions.answer: It shows that an enormous variety is managed all together.

questions.question: What does the short time of five or six weeks suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests great power and perfect control.

questions.question: What does the passage want readers to notice about the way spring happens?
questions.answer: That it comes with precise order and balance.

questions.question: What belief is strengthened by the spring examples of life returning?
questions.answer: Belief in Allah’s power to bring creation back to life.

questions.question: What does the mention of creating the heavens and earth in six days add to the discussion?
questions.answer: It points to Allah’s great creative power from the beginning.

questions.question: How does the change between night and day support the passage’s message?
questions.answer: It shows steady control over the world all the time.

questions.question: Why is knowing people’s hidden thoughts an especially strong proof?
questions.answer: Because it shows Allah’s knowledge reaches even what others cannot see.

questions.question: What does the phrase about all these acts really being one act teach about their source?
questions.answer: It teaches that they come from one source, not many.

questions.question: What kind of being is the Doer described as?
questions.answer: Unique, mighty, glorious, and exalted.

questions.question: According to the passage, what would belief in partners do to the idea of Allah’s perfection?
questions.answer: It would damage it by suggesting imperfection.

questions.question: How does the passage connect partnership with limiting Allah?
questions.answer: It says partnership would put boundaries on His complete reach.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the seriousness of shirk in Allah’s sight?
questions.answer: It is a very grave sin because it dishonors His greatness.

questions.question: What is the central idea of the second truth?
questions.answer: Allah’s acts of lordship fill the universe in a complete and unlimited way.

questions.question: What two things are named as the real bounds on these acts?
questions.answer: Allah’s wisdom and will.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the deeds of the Creator?
questions.answer: They are balanced, wise, clear-sighted, life-giving, orderly, and firm.

questions.question: What is being denied when the passage rejects chance, nature, and blind force?
questions.answer: It denies that they are true makers or controllers of creation.

questions.question: What humble role is left for causes and elements in this passage?
questions.answer: They only serve as outward means under Allah’s command.

questions.question: What does the passage say will come next after introducing the second truth?
questions.answer: It says three examples will be presented.

questions.question: What name does the passage give to the first truth?
questions.answer: The truth of grandeur and sublimity.

questions.question: What does the passage say about managing stars separated by huge distances?
questions.answer: The same Being creates and governs them all together.

questions.question: How does the passage use flowers to show unity in creation?
questions.answer: It says countless flowers of one kind are made across the whole earth in one pattern.

questions.question: What large number of living groups is mentioned in spring?
questions.answer: More than two hundred thousand kinds of plants and animals.

questions.question: What four actions are listed for how these living things are treated?
questions.answer: They are managed, fed, given life, and made distinct and beautiful.

questions.question: What does the passage say is missing from this giant spring activity?
questions.answer: Confusion, defects, and errors are missing from it.

questions.question: Why is spring called a display of many examples of resurrection?
questions.answer: Because many dead-looking things come alive again before people’s eyes.

questions.question: What earlier creation does this spring display help prove?
questions.answer: It helps prove the creation of the heavens and the earth.

questions.question: What regular change in time is mentioned as part of Allah’s control?
questions.answer: The changing of night and day.

questions.question: What does the passage say Allah knows at the same time as running the universe?
questions.answer: The hidden thoughts inside human hearts.

questions.question: What argument is made from saying these are actually one act?
questions.answer: That one single Doer must be doing them.

questions.question: What does the passage say Allah’s greatness does to the idea of a partner?
questions.answer: It leaves no opening for it at all.

questions.question: What would assigning a partner wrongly say about Allah’s power?
questions.answer: It would falsely say His power is weak or in need.

questions.question: What would assigning a partner wrongly say about Allah’s greatness and perfection?
questions.answer: It would falsely say they include fault and defect.

questions.question: What would assigning a partner wrongly say about Allah’s all-reaching rule?
questions.answer: It would falsely act as if His reach has limits.

questions.question: How does the passage judge the idea that Allah could have partners?
questions.answer: It says no healthy mind could think that.

questions.question: Why is shirk presented as a crime against Allah’s dignity?
questions.answer: Because it attacks His glory, greatness, and majesty.

questions.question: What does the Qur’anic statement in the passage teach about forgiveness?
questions.answer: That associating partners with Allah is not forgiven, while lesser sins may be forgiven.

questions.question: What does the second truth focus on?
questions.answer: The complete and universal nature of Allah’s lordly actions in the universe.

questions.question: What keeps these actions measured and fitting, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Allah’s wisdom and will, and the capacities of created things and places.

questions.question: Which explanations are called unable to share in these works?
questions.answer: Chance, nature, blind force, unconscious causes, and scattered elements.

questions.question: Why are those explanations ruled out?
questions.answer: Because they cannot produce works that are so wise, ordered, and full of life.

questions.question: What job do those causes have if they are not real makers?
questions.answer: They are only outward screens used by Allah’s command and power.

questions.question: In simple words, what is the first truth about?
questions.answer: It is about how great and lofty Allah is.

questions.question: Why does the passage not give all the proofs for this truth here?
questions.answer: Because it says those proofs were already explained elsewhere.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the same Being and the faraway stars?
questions.answer: The same Being makes and runs them all together.

questions.question: What example from flowers shows one plan across the globe?
questions.answer: Countless flowers of one species appear in all regions of the earth in the same form.

questions.question: What huge springtime job is described in the passage?
questions.answer: Caring for and organizing over two hundred thousand kinds of plants and animals.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the quality of this springtime job?
questions.answer: It is done with excellent order and balance.

questions.question: What problems does the passage say do not appear in this work?
questions.answer: There is no mix-up, fault, or mistake.

questions.question: Why does the passage connect spring with resurrection?
questions.answer: Because spring shows many living things return after seeming dead.

questions.question: What creation from long ago is mentioned next to this spring sign?
questions.answer: The making of the heavens and the earth in six days.

questions.question: What two parts of the day does Allah join and separate?
questions.answer: Night and day.

questions.question: What does the passage say about Allah and people’s inner thoughts?
questions.answer: He knows and directs even the hidden thoughts in their hearts.

questions.question: What big conclusion comes from all these works being counted as one work?
questions.answer: They all belong to one unique and strong Creator.

questions.question: What does Allah’s majesty make impossible, according to the passage?
questions.answer: It makes having any partner impossible.

questions.question: If someone claims Allah has partners, what insults are included in that claim?
questions.answer: It treats Him as if He has need, weakness, flaws, and limits.

questions.question: What does the passage say a sound intellect would think about that claim?
questions.answer: It would reject it as impossible.

questions.question: Why is shirk called a grave crime here?
questions.answer: Because it goes against Allah’s grandeur, glory, and high rank.

questions.question: What lesson comes from the Qur’anic verse quoted about shirk?
questions.answer: That shirk is more serious than other sins because it is not forgiven.

questions.question: What is the second truth mainly about?
questions.answer: It is about Allah’s actions of care and rule appearing everywhere in the universe.

questions.question: What alone sets the limits for those actions?
questions.answer: Allah’s wisdom and will.

questions.question: What else is mentioned as affecting how those actions appear?
questions.answer: The built-in abilities of the things and places where they appear.

questions.question: Name two false causes the passage says cannot share in these deeds.
questions.answer: Chance and nature.

questions.question: Why can blind force not be the real doer of these acts?
questions.answer: Because these acts are wise, orderly, and life-giving.

questions.question: What does the passage say causes and elements are used for instead?
questions.answer: They are used as an outer veil over Allah’s power.

questions.question: How many examples does the passage promise after this?
questions.answer: Three examples.

questions.question: What is the heading of the first truth in the marked passage?
questions.answer: Grandeur and sublimity.

questions.question: What reason is given for keeping the explanation of the first truth short?
questions.answer: The fuller proofs are said to be in other sections.

questions.question: What does the passage teach by talking about stars that are very distant from each other?
questions.answer: Allah handles even the most far-spread things together with ease.

questions.question: What does the example of one flower species in every direction of the globe show?
questions.answer: It shows one Maker works across the whole earth in the same way.

questions.question: What does the passage say happens to hundreds of thousands of kinds of living things in a few weeks?
questions.answer: They are managed and brought forth with care and order.

questions.question: What does this spring work show about Allah’s control?
questions.answer: It shows control that is exact and free from mistakes.

questions.question: Why are these spring events important for human beings to see?
questions.answer: They are signs in front of people’s eyes of Allah’s power to bring life.

questions.question: Which verse-based example points to the beginning of the world’s creation?
questions.answer: The mention of the heavens and the earth being created in six days.

questions.question: Which verse-based example points to Allah’s constant rule over time?
questions.answer: The joining of night and day into one another.

questions.question: What inward human reality is included under Allah’s knowledge and rule?
questions.answer: The hidden thoughts of the heart.

questions.question: Why does the passage say the many listed actions are really one action?
questions.answer: Because they all come from one Doer.

questions.question: What does that teach about Allah’s oneness?
questions.answer: It teaches that His rule and action are not shared with anyone.

questions.question: How much room does the passage leave for the idea of partners with Allah?
questions.answer: It leaves none at all.

questions.question: What four wrong ideas about Allah are tied to shirk in this passage?
questions.answer: Weakness, need, imperfection, and limitation.

questions.question: How does the passage use reason to reject shirk?
questions.answer: It says any sound mind knows such ideas cannot apply to Allah.

questions.question: Why is shirk called a major offense against Allah?
questions.answer: Because it dishonors His glory and majesty.

questions.question: What does the quoted verse say about sins smaller than shirk?
questions.answer: It says they may be forgiven.

questions.question: What broad subject is named as the second truth?
questions.answer: The complete and unlimited spread of Allah’s lordly deeds in the universe.

questions.question: According to the passage, who decides the bounds of those deeds?
questions.answer: Allah, through His wisdom and will.

questions.question: What created factor is also mentioned in how those deeds appear?
questions.answer: The abilities placed in things and in the places where the deeds show up.

questions.question: What does the passage say about chance as an explanation of creation?
questions.answer: It has no share in such careful and wise works.

questions.question: What does the passage say about unconscious causes and scattered elements?
questions.answer: They cannot take part in these ordered and firm deeds.

questions.question: If they are not true causes, how are they described?
questions.answer: They are only outward means used by Allah.

questions.question: What transition does the passage make at the end of the marked section?
questions.answer: It says three examples will be given from certain verses.
